# V2 artifact sidecar: code quality review, round 3

Verdict: **PASS (static code quality review)**. Zero new actionable findings.

Reviewed the complete current module and bridge, round2-to-round3 source diff, new regression and unchanged earlier assertions against `review-source-snapshot-round3.json`. The prior quality FAIL and round2 static PASS remain retained byte-for-byte. This report also supplies the requested supplemental lint assessment. Compilation, strict Clippy, tests, SDK runtime and full-app gates remain unexecuted by this reviewer.

## Supplemental lint assessment

There is **no `large_enum_variant` or `type_complexity` finding**. `crates/android_tools/Cargo.toml` inherits `[lints] workspace = true`; the workspace explicitly allows `type_complexity` at `Cargo.toml:1163` and `large_enum_variant` at line 1175. `./script/clippy` invokes `--deny warnings`, which does not turn an explicitly allowed lint into a warning. Thus `ArtifactSlot::Present(GeneratedArtifact)` versus `Absent`, and `parse_agp`'s nested tuple result, do not require boxing, lint suppression or a new type solely to satisfy those lints. I have not run Clippy or measured the enum layout; the normal strict wrapper still must pass after authorization.

## Object-only wrapper and derive forwarding

`ObjectOnly<D>` at `generated_artifacts.rs:37` owns the existing deserializer without heap allocation or unsafe code. Its `deserialize_any` calls the underlying `deserialize_map` once. The forwarded Serde entry methods therefore require a map at the current DTO or adjacent-tagged-enum root. `is_human_readable` is forwarded unchanged. Actual field access stays with the underlying MapAccess, so list fields, enum strings, optional scalar tasks and paths retain their ordinary shapes instead of being recursively forced to objects.

Every object wire DTO, both adjacent-tagged enums, and the envelope are covered. `ArtifactKind`, a literal-string enum, intentionally remains a normal derive. The reusable macro at lines60–72 supplies the non-generic trait entries; `CapturedField<T>` has explicit generic trait entries at lines838–847, with the expected separate `Deserialize<'de>` and `Serialize` bounds. The native derives retain unknown-field, duplicate-field, status tagging, camelCase, default and custom-field logic. No second manual schema implementation, JSON round-trip, dynamic trait object or payload clone was added.

I inspected the already installed **locked `serde_derive` 1.0.229** source. `internals/attr.rs:469–474` recognizes remote `Self`; `de.rs:43–59` generates a distinct inherent `deserialize` helper for a remote derive rather than a Deserialize trait implementation; `ser.rs:29–44` does the corresponding inherent serializer helper. Consequently `$name::deserialize(ObjectOnly(deserializer))` and `CapturedField::<T>::deserialize(...)` resolve to those inherent helpers, rather than repeatedly invoking the manual trait methods with nested wrapper types. The serialization forwards likewise target the inherent helper. No unconditional-recursion or expanding-monomorphization issue is apparent from this source-established dispatch. This is an inspection result, not a compiled template or execution result.

The locked `serde_json` 1.0.151 `Value` deserializer's map entry at `src/value/de.rs:472–480` admits only `Value::Object`; positional arrays use the separate struct/sequence path. Thus delegating to the map entry addresses the reported positional shape without replacing genuine list fields. Envelope missing versus present-null handling remains through `present_sidecar`; the record-size guard still precedes deserialization, unrelated Basic fields remain ignored, and complete module equality still precedes the paired validation loop. Version policy, minimum consumer checks, path validation and Java not-applicable checks are unchanged by this round.

## Tests, attribution and preservation

The full round2 27-test source is a **byte-identical prefix** of the current source. One appended regression at `tests/generated_artifacts.rs:766` checks the reported `[valid_sidecar]` envelope and seven nested positional replacements spanning producer/consumer versions, named model rows, captured fields, slots and classpath entries. These cases assert typed Malformed failures while preserving the valid fixture. They target an observable alternate wire shape rather than silently changing expected valid behavior. There are now **28 declared tests**, with no new ignore or should-panic markers. None has been executed by this reviewer.

The two complete original ordering ports and all previous boundary assertions remain unchanged. The attributed Apache originals, license and NOTICE remain intact. The bridge is byte-identical to round2. Basic model sources, original tree tests/fixtures, existing UI and the canonical parity matrix are unchanged. No further original test, Studio root-filtering behavior, Kotlin facet equivalence or UI flow receives completion credit from this review.

Actual normal locked build and unfiltered AndroidTools tests, repository strict Clippy/formatting, fresh official SDK Java/bytecode/custom-field/disabled and null/empty getter probes remain task-owner gates under the root's exclusive lease.
